# 03_vfmdetr_siglip2

*Generated by `report.py`. Every number is read from an artefact file; none is entered by hand.*

This row is compared against row 00 on the same synthetic data. It is **not** a comparison against POGS as published: the authors released no trained POGS checkpoint and no capture scene, so no published baseline exists to measure against.

> **Which models ran in train/track:** This row really substitutes one component in `train` and `track`: the relevancy/alignment encoder is SigLIP2-base (768-d) instead of OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 (512-d). The detector is still DETIC and the features are still DINOv2 ViT-S/14, as in row 00, because VFM-DETR (which would replace both) has no released weights. Differences from row 00 therefore reflect the alignment encoder plus run-to-run variation, not a different detector.

## 2. Capability

| role | model | open-vocab | instance masks | weights |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| detection | `detic` | yes | yes | yes |
| features | `dino_vits14` | **no** | n/a | yes |
| alignment | `siglip2` | yes | n/a | yes |

POGS feeds its detector a `custom_vocab` and requires per-instance masks. A model that cannot accept a text vocabulary cannot serve that contract however fast it is.

**Detector IoU: not run.** Run `bash run.sh validate`, which scores DETIC over the authors' 14 real frames.

**`detic` has no latency figure.** It only loads inside the POGS environment, so `bench.py` cannot time it standalone. Every latency number in section 5a covers the feature and alignment models only.

`frames` is moving frames scored over total frames in the sequence. The error figure is displacement error against the generator's ground truth, averaged only over frames where the object actually moved; stationary frames would dilute it toward zero.

## 6. What was patched, and why

**This row patches POGS.** Stock POGS hardcodes the models it uses, so the substitution is not expressible as configuration:

Stock POGS hardcodes OpenCLIP ViT-B-16 512-d as the relevancy encoder and hardcodes the GaussianField CLIP head to 512. SigLIP2-base is 768-d, so both the encoder selection and the head width are env-gated (POGS_ALIGNMENT_ENCODER=siglip2).
